q: How does HUD define a Qualified Census Tract (QCT) for LIHTC?
truth: A census tract where at least 50% of households have income below 60% of area median gross income (AMGI) OR the poverty rate is at least 25%. (Designations are capped so QCTs hold no more than 20% of the area's population.)

q: What population cap applies to QCT designations in a metro area?
truth: All designated QCTs in an area together may not contain more than 20% of that area's total population.

q: What basis boost does a LIHTC property in a QCT or DDA get?
truth: Eligible basis is increased to 130% of the otherwise eligible basis (IRC 42(d)(5)(B)).
src: IRC section 42(d)(5)(B); HUD User QCT/DDA page https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/qct/qct99home.html

q: What is a Difficult Development Area (DDA)?
truth: Metropolitan or nonmetropolitan areas where construction, land, and utility costs are high relative to area incomes (designated annually by HUD).

q: What percentile of rents do HUD Fair Market Rents represent?
truth: The 40th percentile of gross rents for standard-quality units (24 CFR 888.113), drawn from recent movers.

q: When do new HUD Fair Market Rents take effect each year?
truth: At the start of the federal fiscal year, generally October 1.

q: Within what range can a PHA set its voucher payment standard without HUD approval?
truth: The basic range: 90% to 110% of the published FMR.

q: How is the monthly housing assistance payment (HAP) calculated in the Housing Choice Voucher program?
truth: The lower of (payment standard minus total tenant payment) or (unit gross rent minus total tenant payment).

q: At initial lease-up, what is the maximum share of adjusted income a voucher family may pay toward rent?
truth: The family's share cannot exceed 40 percent of adjusted gross income at initial lease-up.

q: What costs does an FMR include, and what does it exclude?
truth: FMR is gross rent: shelter rent plus all major utilities; excludes telephone, cable/satellite TV, and internet.

q: Which federal regulation governs how Fair Market Rents are established?
Which regulation requires a PHA to determine rent reasonableness for a voucher unit?
truth: 24 CFR 982.507 (rent to owner: reasonable rent).

q: How does HUD define an extremely low-income family?
truth: A very low-income family whose income does not exceed the greater of 30% of area median family income or the federal poverty guidelines (capped at the very low-income limit).

q: What are HUD's very low-income and low-income limits as percentages of area median family income?
truth: Very low-income 50%; low-income 80% of area median family income.

q: How does HUD usually compute the four-person low-income limit from the very low-income limit?
truth: Typically 1.6 times the four-person very low-income limit (80%/50%).

q: Over how many years are LIHTC credits claimed?
truth: Ten years (the credit period).

q: How long is the LIHTC initial compliance period?
truth: 15 years, beginning with the first taxable year of the credit period.

q: What is the minimum total affordability period (extended use) for LIHTC properties allocated after 1989?
truth: At least 30 years (15-year compliance period plus extended use).

q: What are the two classic LIHTC minimum set-aside tests?
truth: 20-50 (at least 20% of units at or below 50% AMI) and 40-60 (at least 40% of units at or below 60% AMI).

q: What is the LIHTC income averaging set-aside?
truth: Added by the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2018: at least 40% of units, designated at 20%-80% AMI in 10-point increments, with average designation at or below 60% AMI.

q: What is the maximum gross rent on a LIHTC-restricted unit?
truth: 30% of the imputed income limitation (e.g., 30% of 60% AMI for a 60% unit), including a utility allowance.

q: What present value of qualified cost do 9% and 4% LIHTC credits roughly yield?
truth: 9% credits yield about 70% present value of eligible costs; 4% credits about 30%.

q: What did the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act do to 9% LIHTC allocations?
truth: Permanently increased states' 9% LIHTC allocation authority by 12% starting in 2026.

q: What did the One Big Beautiful Bill Act change about the 4% LIHTC bond financing test?
truth: Permanently lowered the tax-exempt private activity bond threshold from 50% to 25% of aggregate basis for buildings placed in service after Dec 31, 2025 (with at least 5% financed by bonds issued after that date).

q: What financing makes a LIHTC project eligible for the automatic 4% credit?
truth: Financing with tax-exempt private activity bonds (meeting the bond test, now 25% of aggregate basis).

q: What is the current NSPIRE compliance date for the Housing Choice Voucher program?
truth: February 1, 2027 (extended from October 1, 2025 by the Sept 30, 2025 notice; PHAs may keep using HQS until then).

q: When was the NSPIRE final rule published and what does it replace?
truth: Published May 11, 2023 (88 FR 30442); it replaces the older inspection standards (UPCS and HQS definitions) with National Standards for the Physical Inspection of Real Estate.

q: When does HUD begin scoring the new NSPIRE affirmative requirements in property inspection scores?
truth: October 1, 2026.

q: What is a success-rate payment standard in the voucher program?
truth: A payment standard set between 90% and 110% of the 50th percentile rent (not the 40th) with HUD approval when 40th-percentile FMRs produced low lease-up rates.

q: What is the minimum public housing flat rent relative to FMR?
truth: Flat rents must be at least 80% of FMR.

q: What is each state's 2026 LIHTC per-capita 9% credit allocation and small-state minimum?
truth: Greater of $3.416 per capita or a small-state minimum of $3,953,600 (IRS 2026 figures).

q: In the Spain Terminal, what letter grade does a property with a score of 66 get?
What properties make up the Spain Terminal's scorable multifamily universe?

q: In the terminal, does a property being 'scored' mean its inputs are real?
truth: No. 'Scored' means the model ran; inputs may be missing or modeled, so the score is not proof that data was real.

q: What is the current scoring model version in the Spain Terminal?

What share of terminal properties have no rent signal source recorded?
